chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Bunnān ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥassin ibn Aḥmad, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about a man who sees blood on his garment while he is performing ṭawāf. He said: 'He should identify the spot where he saw the blood, then he exits, washes it, then returns and completes his ṭawāf.'

key_terms.يُعَرِّفُهُ: Identify or mark the specific spot

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they find blood on their clothes while performing Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor impurity (najāsah) on clothing does not invalidate the ṭawāf, provided it is removed before the ritual concludes. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that ṭawāf remains valid despite minor impurities, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements for the prayer (ṣalāh). The instruction to wash the specific spot highlights the practical application of purification (ṭahārah) within the continuous flow of the ritual circumambulation.
